label: February 9–15
title: “Noah Found Grace in the Eyes of the Lord” —  Genesis 6

items.text: The story of Noah and the Flood, as well as the Tower of Babel, are incredibly relevant to our day. The scriptures describe Noah’s time as filled with corruption and violence, much like our present society. These ancient accounts offer vital lessons on how to navigate and find safety amidst wickedness, teaching us what to do when faced with similar challenges.

When Jesus Christ taught about His Second Coming, He likened the signs of the times to the days of Noah. Understanding the corruption and violence prevalent in Noah’s era, and the pride and confusion that led to the Tower of Babel, helps us recognize patterns that can repeat throughout history and even in our own lives.

Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord, and his family was protected from the confusion and division that plagued Babel. These narratives are not just historical accounts of wickedness repeating itself, but powerful teachings on how to find spiritual safety and protection. They demonstrate the Lord’s desire to guide us through perilous times.

There is profound spiritual safety in following the Lord’s prophet. Just as God called Noah to warn and guide his people, He calls a prophet today. The modern prophet warns us of dangers and invites us to follow Christ, offering guidance that helps us remain safe amidst the corruption and violence of our times.

Elder Allen D. Haynie taught that a perfect and loving Father in Heaven reveals truth through a prophet. Having a living prophet is a testament to God’s love for His children. Studying the messages of our prophet can help us understand the warnings and invitations relevant to our lives and feel secure in following divine guidance.

The Flood, while seemingly a destructive act, was an act of God’s mercy. Elder Neal A. Maxwell explained that corruption had reached a point where sending spirits to earth would not be just. The Lord’s tender mercy and love are evident even in His judgments, as He sought to preserve life and offer a new beginning.

The rainbow, a token from God, serves as a reminder of His covenants. It brings to mind His promises and His love. We can identify other symbols and objects God has given us to help us remember our covenants, which teach us invaluable lessons and strengthen our connection to Him.

Following Jesus Christ is the singular path to returning to Heavenly Father. The people of Babel sought to reach heaven through their own prideful efforts, resulting in confusion. In contrast, the people of Zion achieved heaven through righteousness and obedience to God’s will, highlighting the importance of His provided path.

God has provided the Savior, Jesus Christ, to help us reach unto heaven. The account of the Tower of Babel contrasts with the building of Zion, illustrating two distinct ways individuals attempt to ascend. One is built on pride and self-reliance, the other on faith and divine guidance through the Savior.

The scriptures teach us that the Lord calls prophets to warn and guide His people. Noah was called to warn of the Flood, and our living prophet warns us of spiritual dangers. By listening to and following the prophet, we can find spiritual safety and protection in the latter days, just as Noah did.
